newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-One regulator says Australia's State Bank NSW.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-One regulator says Australia's State Bank NSW.

text.p: Australia's State Bank of New South Wales (NSW) chairman Peter Smedley said on Friday that his organisation favoured one prudential regulator for financial and insurance institutions.

"We would clearly see a need for what some people would describe as a mega-regulator," Smedley told reporters when asked about the bank's submission to the Wallis inquiry into regulation in the Australian financial sector.
"What we don't have is a regulator that can look at our organisation and see us as an integrated financial organisation."

Smedley said a single regulator, with different institutional supervisory streams under the one umbrella, was necessary because of the convergence of banking, funds management and insurance industries into the one bancassurance market.
Banks and insurance companies now have different regulators.
Earlier the bank announced that profit after tax rose to A$52 million in the six months to June 30 from A$49.7 million the previous corresponding period.
State Bank is owned by Colonial Mutual Life Assurance Society Ltd, which plans to list within the next 12 months.
Smedley said while Colonial's demutualisation was anticipated to be completed by the end of calendar 1996, he was unable to specify a time frame for listing on the Australian Stock Exchange.
"We were targetting demutualisation by the end of this year and we anticipate that subject to our members agreeing, and the courts endorsing that, that we will be on schedule," he said.
"Listing will follow at an appropriate time. We would like to do it as soon as possible, quite obviously, from a management point of view, but we need to take into account many things."
